title: Turn a product brief into a GenAI architecture
description: Choose a workload, model tier, and execution path. The lab checks whether the design satisfies the declared requirements without treating a larger model as an automatic solution.
evidenceNote: Latency values are synthetic planning measurements for this lesson. Replace them with traces from your own candidate models and deployment path.

scenarios.label: Employee support answer
scenarios.detail: Answer policy questions from permission-filtered internal documents and cite the evidence.
scenarios.userOutcome: A grounded answer or an explicit insufficient-evidence response

scenarios.label: Insurance claim investigation
scenarios.detail: Review documents, retrieve policy evidence, and prepare a proposed action for an adjuster.
scenarios.userOutcome: An evidence-linked recommendation that cannot execute without approval

scenarios.label: Catalog copy draft
scenarios.detail: Create short product descriptions from structured attributes for later editorial review.
scenarios.userOutcome: A schema-valid draft that preserves supplied product facts

tiers.label: Compact tier
tiers.detail: Lowest planning latency; suitable for bounded transformations that pass task-specific evaluation.

tiers.label: Balanced tier
tiers.detail: Supports broader instructions and image input at a moderate planning envelope.

tiers.label: Deliberate tier
tiers.detail: Reserves more model work for complex, high-value tasks when measured quality justifies it.

architectures.label: Prompt-only generation
architectures.detail: The application supplies bounded request data directly to the model.

architectures.label: Retrieval-assisted answer
architectures.detail: The application authorizes and retrieves evidence before generation, then checks citations.

architectures.label: Governed tool workflow
architectures.detail: The model proposes bounded tool calls; deterministic policy and approval gates own execution.
